newsitem.title: GERMANY: Crucifixes must stay in Bavarian schools - court.
newsitem.headline: Crucifixes must stay in Bavarian schools - court.

text.p: Bavaria's supreme court on Friday upheld a 1995 law that requires schools in the fervently Roman Catholic state in southern Germany to hang crucifixes or crosses on classroom walls.

Rejecting a legal challenge by a religious freedom pressure group and a number of individuals, the Bavarian constitutional court ruled that the 1995 law did not violate the principle of religious neutrality enshrined in the federal constitution.

The ruling was a victory for Roman Catholics in Bavaria who have been up in arms since the cherished practice, which is unique in Germany, was ruled unconstitutional by the Federal Constitutional Court.
Some had even compared the federal court's ruling to attempts by the Nazis during World War Two to replace the crucifix with portraits of Adolf Hitler.
Bavaria's ruling Christian Social Union (CSU) hailed the decision to uphold the state law, which the party helped push through the regional assembly two years ago.
"The issue of whether the Bavarian regulation violates the federal constitution is finally off the agenda," Bavarian premier Edmund Stoiber said in a statement.
But opponents of the law said the battle was not over.
They slammed the ruling, saying it violated the rights of minority religious groups, and vowed to take their case to the Federal Constitutional Court, the highest court in the land.
The head of the Association for Religious Freedom, Gerhard Rampp, accused the Bavarian supreme court of placing "political and philosophical allegiances above judicial expertise".

The Bavarian law of 1995 reinstated a long-standing edict that schools must hang crucifixes or crosses in classrooms, but qualified this by saying parents or children who objected could reach an "amicable agreement" with school authorities.
Bavaria drafted the new law after the Federal Constitutional Court upheld a complaint from a family living in Bavaria, who were followers of Austrian philosopher Rudolf Steiner.
The family had campaigned for 10 years to have the crosses removed after a crucifix terrified their daughter on her first day at school.

Tens of thousands of Bavarian Christians took to the streets in protest against the Federal Constitutional Court's ruling and Chancellor Helmut Kohl was among a host of German public figures who also denounced the decision.
